title: Formalize self-duality of Desargues theorem in projective geometry

problemStatement.formal: dual(perspFromPoint) = perspFromLine ∧ Desargues identity symmetric under triangle swap
problemStatement.plain: Self-duality of Desargues's theorem: in homogeneous coordinates, collinearity and concurrence are the same predicate, so the dual configuration's perspective-from-a-point equals the original's perspective-from-a-line. The Desargues identity is symmetric under triangle swap.
whyMatters: Projective duality is a cornerstone of projective geometry
Self-duality makes Desargues the premier example of the duality principle
Shows duality is definitional in homogeneous coordinates, not a deep theorem

insights: In homogeneous coordinates, collinear and concurrent are DEFINITIONALLY the same predicate (det=0). This makes self-duality trivial.
The Desargues identity det(P,Q,R) = det(AA',BB',CC')·det(ABC)·det(A'B'C') is manifestly symmetric since det(ABC)·det(A'B'C') commutes.
Cross product anticommutativity means swap negates each row, giving factor (-1)^3=-1 in determinant. But -0=0 preserves the zero condition.
